priced_in_summary: Not TOO_LATE, and the reason it is not is worth stating because the surface facts point that way. A +37.35% twelve-month move that is 100% multiple expansion on falling revenue and falling net income, with the price 0.72% under its 52-week high and at the sell-side average target, is the textbook shape of a re-rating that ate its runway (method section 2). What stops this dive calling it is that the multiple expanded against real new forward numbers rather than against a story: H1 2026 group order intake +25.2% to 5.9bn EUR, order backlog a record 12,602.1 MEUR (+20.5% versus year-end 2025, or 1.60x FY2025 revenue), Hydropower intake 2,445.9 MEUR in six months against 2,516.1 MEUR for the whole of record-year 2025. For a plant engineer the order book IS the estimate revision, so the decomposition method section 7 demands does not show story-over-numbers; it shows a multiple that moved because the forward numbers moved. That is ordinary correct pricing, and the verdict for correct pricing is WATCH, not TOO_LATE. AMENDED by the red team 2026-09-02, on both halves and in opposite directions. First, the draft substituted 'for a plant engineer the order book IS the estimate revision' for the quantity method section 7 actually names, and never measured estimate revisions. Measured, they moved: consensus target raised to 87 EUR from 82.83 EUR with 13 analysts lifting on 2026-07-31, and the most recent reported period is not falling at all (H1 2026 'Revenue increases by 5.2%' and 'net income increased to 201.0 MEUR (+4.9% vs. H1 2025: 191.6 MEUR)'). The 'falling revenue and falling net income' framing is true of FY2025 against FY2024 and false of the latest half-year, and the +45.4% price-to-sales expansion is partly a denominator artifact of rolling the latest reported annual revenue from FY2024's 8,313.7 MEUR down to FY2025's 7,883.1 MEUR. So the decomposition genuinely does not show story-over-numbers, and declining TOO_LATE now rests on a measurement rather than an assertion. Second, and against the dive: the surge that justified the re-rating is one quarter and has already reversed (see bull[0] as amended), and the like-for-like gap flips sign under a convention the draft never named (see the net_gap_direction row as amended). The verdict is unchanged and the reasons on both sides are stronger than the draft's.

bull.point: The order book moved harder than anything in the P&L, and for a long-cycle plant engineer the order book is the forward estimate. H1 2026 group order intake rose 25.2% to 5.9 billion EUR, the order backlog reached a record 12,602.1 MEUR, +20.5% against year-end 2025 and 1.60x FY2025 revenue of 7,883.1 MEUR, and Hydropower order intake alone was 2,445.9 MEUR, +81.8% against 1,345.4 MEUR in H1 2025 and within 3% of the whole of FY2025's own record 2,516.1 MEUR in half the time. That is contracted work, not a forecast. AMENDED by the red team 2026-09-02, and this bullet is materially weaker than it was written: 76.7% of the H1 Hydropower intake landed in the FIRST quarter. Q1 2026 hydro order intake was 1,876.8 MEUR (+229.9% vs Q1 2025: 568.9 MEUR), which leaves Q2 2026 at 569.1 MEUR against Q2 2025's 776.5 MEUR, DOWN 26.7% year on year. The +81.8% half-year headline is therefore one lumpy quarter of very large awards followed by a quarter below the prior year, not a demand regime evidenced over two periods. The named orders behind it are Saidongar in India (3,000 MW), Tata Power's Bhivpuri (1,000 MW), projects in Southeast Asia and Brazil, and pumped-storage work in Austria and France: no Chinese content, so not one euro of this order book is traceable to the occurrence that put ANDRITZ on this chain.

red_team.surviving_bear_case: What survives is a company whose thesis rests on a single quarter. Three quarters of the H1 2026 Hydropower order surge landed in Q1 (1,876.8 MEUR of 2,445.9) and Q2's 569.1 MEUR came in 26.7% below the same quarter of 2025, so the +81.8% half-year headline that carries this dive is one lumpy quarter of very large pumped-storage awards in India, Southeast Asia, Brazil, Austria and France, none of it traceable to the Chinese occurrence that put ANDRITZ on this chain at all. Converting that book shifts mix toward the group's lowest-margin business (6.5% Hydropower EBITA against 8.2% group in FY2025), H1 2026 already printed a comparable margin of 8.6% against the company's own 8.7% guided floor, and the price has already paid for the good version: +37.35% in twelve months, all of it multiple expansion, 0.72% under the 52-week high, with the gap against the filed 5.3% implied ask measuring +0.19pp on the dive's own build and MINUS 1.85pp once cash conversion comes off its FY2025 point and onto its four-year mean. And none of it can be audited: the one balance-sheet line that would show whether the cash is earned or advanced by customers, contract liabilities, is absent from the only source this repo holds, which is why the earnings grade is NULL, why nothing on this page is verified against a primary document, and why a cheaper price would not change the verdict.
